args.summary: checkout-api (v2.3.1) began failing health checks after the latest deploy, with an elevated error rate (~18%) across all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). SRE rolled back the service to v2.3.0, the most recent version that was healthy in production, in all regions. Rollback completed successfully and service health is being verified.
args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
Done. Here's a summary:

- **Diagnosis**: checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an ~18% error rate.
- **Rollback**: Rolled back to **v2.3.0** — the most recent release with a healthy status in production — across all regions. Rollback completed successfully.
- **Verification**: Service is now **healthy** on v2.3.0 with an error rate of ~0.2%.
- **Incident**: Opened SEV2 incident **INC-0001** ("checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0"), describing the failure, the rollback action, and the verification. The on-call engineer has been paged.

No change-manager approval was needed since v2.3.0 was previously healthy in production.

transcript.content: I'll start by checking the service status and deployment history to identify the latest healthy release.

transcript.content: The service is unhealthy on v2.3.1; the most recent healthy production release is **v2.3.0**. I'll roll back to that now.

Both could be parallel but the incident should mention the completed rollback — better to roll back first, then create the incident. The rollback must complete before describing it. I'll do rollback first.
